title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Budget cut and US-China rivalry
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce Head N of the Estimates by $100, and US-China rivalry is named a key source of geopolitical uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100." A key source of geopolitical uncertainty is the growing United States (US)-China rivalry.

sections.label: Semiconductor supply chains and trade restrictions
sections.summary: Singapore's semiconductor industry could be impacted by measures not targeted at Singapore, amid trade restrictions and sanctions by both countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While these measures are not targeted at Singapore, our semiconductor industry could potentially be impacted, given the highly complex nature of semi-conductor supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In a more general dial-back of trade liberalisation, the last few years have seen both countries announce trade restrictions and sanctions against entities and individuals on both sides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We can expect more intense and vigorous competition between both powers in the years ahead.

sections.label: Risk of escalatory spiral
sections.summary: Nationalistic rhetoric on both sides means miscalculation or accident could lead to an escalatory spiral and destabilise the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While the US and China are not actively looking for conflict, the nationalistic rhetoric on both sides means that there is a real danger that any miscalculation or accident could potentially lead to an escalatory spiral and destabilise our region.

sections.label: Singapore engagement and National Day Rally
sections.summary: A question is asked on how Singapore has engaged the US and China, noting the Prime Minister's National Day Rally assessment of US-China relations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: How has Singapore engaged both the US and China on their strategic rivalry?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Prime Minister’s National Day Rally last year outlined perhaps the most pessimistic assessment of US-China relations in recent memory.

sections.label: Geopolitical contestation and choosing sides
sections.summary: The Prime Minister noted more geopolitical contestation was likely in the Asia Pacific and that some countries would choose a side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister noted that more geopolitical contestation was likely in the Asia Pacific and that some countries would choose a side.

sections.label: Taiwan question and choosing sides
sections.summary: A question is asked on how the Ministry assesses the Taiwan question and whether it will force Singapore to choose a side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry assess the Taiwan question?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is it a red line and will it force Singapore to choose a side?

sections.label: Singaporeans first, ethnic realities
sections.summary: It states Singaporeans should be called Singaporeans first while honouring ethnic and racial realities, to prepare psychologically for unpredictable US-China relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should not shy away from saying that we are Singaporeans first, while recognising and honouring our ethnic and racial realities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This distinction would be critical in building up our psychological readiness for unpredictable US-China relations.

sections.label: Singapore-China November 2022 events
sections.summary: It describes November 2022 Singapore-China events: the 18th JCBC in Singapore signing 19 MOUs and Agreements, and a Xi Jinping-Lee Hsien Loong APEC meeting in Bangkok.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, November 2022 was one of the months when we saw two important events taking place and boosted the relationship between Singapore and China.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There was the 18th Joint Council of Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) that was held in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This meeting was co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister of Economic Policies, Mr Heng Swee Keat and the Vice Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, Mr Han Zheng.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A total of 19 Memoranda of Understandings (MOUs) and Agreements were signed with both countries agreeing to continue to work to look for growth opportunities in areas, such as digital and green economies to collaborate in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Shortly after that, in the same month, Chinese President, Mr Xi Jinping and our Prime Minister, Mr Lee Hsien Loong, met on the sidelines of the 29th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders' Meeting in Bangkok.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: After months of strict lockdowns in China, China has now abandoned its zero COVID-19 policy and reopened its border.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia relations new chapter
sections.summary: It says the event opens a new chapter in Singapore-Malaysia relations, with progress on the FIR, Rapid Transit System and Causeway congestion, and notes deep ties and trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The event marks a new chapter in relations across the Singapore Strait, one where our two countries can, perhaps, continue putting down some of the historical baggage accumulated over the years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the fact that Singapore and Putrajaya are moving ahead on such issues as management of the Flight Information Region (FIR), development of the Rapid Transit System and reducing congestion along the Causeway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The histories of our countries are deeply intertwined, family and social ties link our societies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We are consistently among each other's largest trading partners and Singapore is one of the main sources of foreign direct investment (FDI) into Malaysia – in fact, second largest in 2021.

sections.label: Frameworks and MOUs signed
sections.summary: It states Prime Minister Anwar and Prime Minister Lee witnessed the signing of Frameworks and MOUs on Digital Economy, Green Economy, and Personal Data Protection, Cybersecurity and Digital Economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Anwar and Prime Minister Lee also witnessed the signing of several Frameworks and MOUs, including Frameworks on Cooperation in Digital Economy and Green Economy, and an MOU on Personal Data Protection, Cybersecurity and Digital Economy.

sections.label: Singapore top FDI source Indonesia
sections.summary: It states Singapore has consistently been Indonesia's top source of foreign direct investment since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore has consistently been Indonesia's top source of FDI since 2014.

sections.label: Indonesia ratifies Expanded Framework agreements
sections.summary: It states Indonesia's 2022 ratification of all three agreements on FIR, Defence Cooperation and Fugitives Extradition under the Expanded Framework showed the relationship's strength and maturity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the bilateral front, Indonesia's ratification of all three agreements, covering FIR, Defence Cooperation and Fugitives Extradition, under the Expanded Framework between Singapore and Indonesia in 2022, was a clear sign of the strength and maturity of our relationship and our commitment to work together as close neighbours.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat agreements
sections.summary: In January 2022, Lee and Widodo witnessed agreements on three bilateral issues under an Expanded Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Last year, Prime Minister Lee and Indonesian Prime Minister Joko Widodo held their Leaders' Retreat in January 2022 in Indonesia, where they witnessed a set of agreements on three long-standing bilateral issues under an Expanded Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: They were an Agreement on the Realignment of the Boundary between the Jakarta FIR and the Singapore FIR, a Treaty for the Extradition of Fugitives, and a Joint Statement between the Defence Ministers on the 2007 Defence Cooperation Agreement.

sections.label: Flight Information Region boundaries
sections.summary: The FIR sets out agreed boundaries, with Indonesia delegating responsibility to Singapore for 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The FIR sets out the agreed boundaries between Singapore and Indonesia in responsibilities for the FIR, with Indonesia delegating responsibility to Singapore for 25 years to provide continuity with what is going on today.

sections.label: Extradition treaty and ratification
sections.summary: The extradition treaty lists extraditable offences and formalises existing practices; Indonesia ratified all three treaties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The extradition treaty provides for a complete list of extraditable offences between Singapore and Indonesia and builds on and formalises existing practices, where law enforcement agencies already cooperate with each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In January this year, MFA announced that Indonesia had ratified all three treaties.

sections.label: Regional grouping's role
sections.summary: The regional grouping fosters social, cultural and economic ties, enhances stability and integrates Southeast Asian economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The regional grouping plays an important role in fostering deeper social, cultural and economic ties, enhancing regional stability and integrating Southeast Asian economies.

sections.label: ASEAN consultation and consensus
sections.summary: A key tenet of ASEAN requires decision-making by consultation and consensus, giving any member veto power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A key tenet of ASEAN is the requirement for decision-making to be based on "consultation and consensus", effectively giving any member the veto power over decisions.

sections.label: ASEAN Charter Article 20
sections.summary: Article 20 of the ASEAN Charter states that where consensus cannot be achieved, the ASEAN Summit may decide how a decision can be made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to Article 20 of the ASEAN Charter, "where a consensus cannot be achieved, the ASEAN Summit may decide how a specific decision can be made".

sections.label: Myanmar ASEAN Five-Point Consensus
sections.summary: Little progress has been achieved by the Myanmar Armed Forces in implementing ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus after the military coup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, little progress has been achieved by the Myanmar Armed Forces in the implementation of ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus to put Myanmar back on the path to peace following the military coup.

sections.label: India Singapore PayNow UPI Linkage
sections.summary: The PayNow-UPI Linkage launched by Prime Minister Lee and Prime Minister Modi allows cheaper, faster, safer cross-border retail payments and remittances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Given this blistering pace of growth, it is imperative that Singapore does more to engage our giant Asian neighbour for mutual benefit, not just between the countries but also ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I was happy to note an initiative that Prime Minister Mr Narendra Modi from India suggested in 2018 when he visited Singapore was made reality on 21 February 2023, when Prime Minister Lee and Prime Minister Modi both launched the PayNow-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Linkage that will allow for cheaper, faster and safer cross-border retail payments and remittances for businesses and individuals.

sections.label: Singapore-UK Third Country Training Programme
sections.summary: Mr James Cleverly and Dr Vivian Balakrishnan signed a MOU on the Singapore-UK Third Country Training Programme last September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Chairman, the UK Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, Mr James Cleverly, and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, signed a MOU on the Singapore-UK Third Country Training Programme (TCTP) last September.

sections.label: Germany-Singapore Sustainability and Innovation Framework
sections.summary: The German Federal Chancellor's official visit last November concluded with the signing of the Germany-Singapore Framework for Sustainability and Innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: The Federal Chancellor of Germany made an official visit to Singapore last November, which concluded with the signing of the Germany-Singapore Framework for Sustainability and Innovation which aims to increase economic partnership.

sections.label: GCC-Singapore Free Trade Agreement
sections.summary: Both sides noted the GCC-Singapore Free Trade Agreement, in force since 2013, and encouraged greater exchanges in areas like food security and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Both sides noted the strong foundation for cooperation set in place by the GCC-Singapore Free Trade Agreement, which entered into force in 2013 and encouraged greater exchanges between the GCC and Singapore, as well as with ASEAN in areas of mutual interest, like food security and education.

sections.label: Major Power Rivalry and Decoupling
sections.summary: Major power rivalry and the Ukraine war have altered the global geopolitical landscape, with countries taking unilateral decoupling actions in trade, technology, investments and finance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The rivalry and intensification of competition between major powers and the Ukraine war has altered the global geopolitical landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are increasingly seeing countries taking unilateral actions to decouple in areas of trade, technology, investments and finance.

sections.label: Geopolitics, trade groups, ageing populations
sections.summary: Geopolitical clashes, regional trading groups and ageing populations in developed countries have caused inflation and slowed economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Three, the combination of geopolitical clashes, the formation of regional trading groups and the ageing of populations in developed countries have caused inflation and slowed down economic growth.

sections.label: Evacuation and aid for Singaporeans
sections.summary: MFA and missions helped stranded Singaporeans during the Wuhan lockdown in 2020 and the Shanghai lockdown in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: When Wuhan city was dramatically locked down in January 2020, MFA and our embassy in Beijing were in touch with stranded Singaporeans there and worked on their expeditious evacuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: Similarly, when Shanghai went into lockdown mode in April 2022, our Consulate-General office in Shanghai sent food packs to Singaporeans who were unable to obtain food on their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: They also helped source for essential supplies and medications, and facilitated Singaporeans who wished to return home urgently.

sections.label: SCP courses and climate governance
sections.summary: Close to 150,000 foreign officials attended SCP courses, and MFA launched the Sustainability Action Package for developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Close to 150,000 foreign officials have participated in SCP courses, and a large proportion of participants were from ASEAN member states.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the commitment from countries is strong in wanting to reduce global emissions under the Paris Agreement, there needs to be demonstrated political will to set up intersectoral climate governance on critical areas like renewable energy transition, food security, forest and land use protection amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I note that MFA has launched the Sustainability Action Package (SAP) to support the capacity-building needs of developing countries on sustainability and climate change.

sections.label: Domestic consensus on foreign policy
sections.summary: The Foreign Minister said diplomacy is credible only with domestic consensus on Singapore's core interests and foreign policy priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In a speech in July 2017, the Foreign Minister stated that "our diplomacy is only credible, if we are able to maintain a domestic consensus on Singapore's core interests and our foreign policy priorities." If there is insufficient engagement with Singaporeans on foreign policy, it will be close to impossible to build and maintain that "domestic consensus", especially in the face of a plethora of news and information from abroad, including disinformation.

sections.label: Manpower Development budget equality allocation
sections.summary: The question asks how much of the approximately $10 million for Manpower Development in MFA's FY2023 Budget goes to equality efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How much of the approximately $10 million earmarked for "Manpower Development" in MFA's FY2023 Budget is allocated to equality efforts?

sections.label: Singapore's ranking among UNHCR donors
sections.summary: In 2021, Singapore ranked 103rd on a list of 125 donors to the UNHCR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2021, Singapore ranked 103rd on a list of 125 donors to the UNHCR.

sections.label: ASEAN contribution increase six years ago
sections.summary: The contribution was increased by $10,000 six years ago, to US$60,000 annually now, and is comparable to other ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that and I also appreciate that our contribution is comparable to that of other ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been six years since we increased our contributions by $10,000, to US$60,000 annually now.

sections.label: Non-Resident Ambassadors and consular demands
sections.summary: It asks whether scholarships could be extended to refugees and about resources for Non-Resident Ambassadors, noting 2022's visits and consular demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider following the Philippines and extending scholarships to a limited number of refugees?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Non-Resident Ambassadors (NRAs) are a unique part of Singapore's diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scheme widens the MFA's reach beyond countries in which we have a permanent mission and helps to build personal diplomatic relations with a larger number of countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Further, could I also enquire on the resources that are made available to enable them to carry out their duties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have also noticed that most of the NRAs have private emails, some even Gmail accounts listed on the Singapore Government directory online and on MFA's website.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, 2022 was a very busy year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We handled close to 200 incoming and outgoing visits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The demand for consular services will intensify as more Singaporeans travel overseas and sometimes get into trouble.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But more critically, the world has become much more complex, with a perfect storm of multiple interlocking crises in the military, security, economic, public health, climate, technological and sociopolitical domains.

sections.label: Foreign policy based on national interests
sections.summary: Foreign policy must be based on Singapore's long-term national interests and vulnerabilities, refusing to be a vassal, proxy or stalking horse, and not choosing sides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Second point, our foreign policy must be based on a clear-eyed understanding of Singapore's long-term national interests and our vulnerabilities in a volatile and dangerous world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We refuse to be a vassal state that can be bullied or bought.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will not be a proxy or a stalking horse for any superpower.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will uphold principles, but we will not choose sides.

sections.label: Taiwan Strait dangerous flashpoint
sections.summary: The Taiwan Strait has become a more dangerous flashpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Taiwan Strait has become a more dangerous flashpoint.

sections.label: Taiwan conflict impact on Singapore
sections.summary: A conflict over Taiwan will have global repercussions and a more direct impact on Singapore than the war in Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A conflict over Taiwan will have global repercussions and a much more direct impact on Singapore than the ongoing war in Ukraine.

sections.label: Expanded Framework agreements with Indonesia
sections.summary: Singapore and Indonesia completed domestic legal processes to ratify the FIR Agreement, Defence Cooperation Agreement and Extradition Treaty, to enter into force simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about the significance of the Expanded Framework agreements with Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that Singapore and Indonesia recently completed our respective domestic legal processes for the ratification of the three agreements under the Expanded Framework, namely the FIR Agreement, the Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA), and the Extradition Treaty (ET).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Once the FIR Agreement is ready for implementation, both sides will arrange for all three agreements to enter into force simultaneously, on a mutually agreed date.

sections.label: Border crossing project and Pedra Branca
sections.summary: A two-way border travel project is expected to start operations by end-2026, while Malaysia objects to Singapore's Pedra Branca development works.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This project will facilitate more convenient two-way travel for the tens of thousands who cross the border every day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is making good progress and is expected to commence operations by the end of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For example, while the issue of sovereignty over Pedra Branca has been conclusively settled, Malaysia has raised objections to Singapore's development works at Pedra Branca.

sections.label: Suspension of Pedra Branca works
sections.summary: Singapore suspended works in May 2022 for discussions on Malaysia's concerns and in December 2022 proposed ways to resolve the issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, in the spirit of mutual cooperation and good faith, we temporarily suspended the works in May 2022, to facilitate discussions on Malaysia's concerns and to comprehensively address Malaysia's queries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In December 2022, Singapore put forward proposals to Malaysia to resolve the issue and move forward with the works.

sections.label: ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships
sections.summary: ASEAN upgraded relations with the US and India to Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships, after doing the same with China and Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Last year, ASEAN upgraded its relations with the US and India to Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships, after doing the same with China and Australia the year before.

sections.label: Timor-Leste ASEAN accession assistance
sections.summary: Singapore committed to assisting Timor-Leste's ASEAN accession, to be achieved through an objective, criteria-based roadmap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore has also committed to assisting Timor-Leste in its accession to ASEAN membership, which is to be achieved through an objective, criteria-based roadmap.

sections.label: UN Charter and Russia's invasion
sections.summary: The UN Charter enshrines peaceful dispute settlement, non-use of force and non-interference, and Russia's invasion jeopardises small states' security and existence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The UN Charter enshrines the core principles of peaceful settlement of disputes, the non-use of force and non-interference in a country's internal affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Russia's invasion sets a very dangerous precedent that jeopardises the security and existence of small states, and especially small states like us.

sections.label: Carbon market negotiations and agreements
sections.summary: Singapore co-facilitated Article 6 carbon market negotiations at COP and concluded carbon market collaboration agreements with Ghana, Peru and Papua New Guinea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore has been co-facilitating Article 6 negotiations on developing carbon markets at the Conference of Parties (COP) of the United Nations Framework Climate Change (UNFCCC) and concluded carbon market collaboration agreements with Ghana, Peru and Papua New Guinea at COP27 last year.

sections.label: Digital and green economy agreements
sections.summary: Singapore signed DEPA with Chile and New Zealand, is reviewing accession requests, and signed the Singapore-Australia Green Economy Agreement in October 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, we have signed the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) with Chile and New Zealand, and in fact, right now, this agreement with only three small countries – Chile, New Zealand and Singapore – we are now reviewing accession requests from the ROK, China, Canada and Costa Rica.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We signed the landmark Singapore-Australia Green Economy Agreement in October 2022, the first-of-its-kind agreement that will facilitate trade and investment in environmentally sustainable goods and services, and such collaborations are crucial as we work towards keeping Singapore sustainable and economically vibrant.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia high-level visits
sections.summary: There have been over 10 high-level visits since the year's start, with more planned, including President Halimah's state visit to Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Since the start of the year, there have been more than 10 high-level visits, including by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: President Halimah will make a state visit to Malaysia next month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Apart from the visit by Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi earlier this month, we also hosted delegations from Terengganu, Selangor and Sarawak.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I will be visiting Terengganu and Kelantan in April – to explore opportunities to work together for mutual benefit.

sections.label: Teacher and religious exchanges with Malaysia
sections.summary: Malay Language teachers engaged UPSI counterparts through the E-Immersion Programme, and MUIS hosted Perak religious authorities led by Mufti Dr Wan Zahidi Wan Teh.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Teachers are also encouraged to build their professional networks with their Malaysian counterparts, through the E-Immersion Programme, which saw more than 30 Malay Language teachers and pedagogical leaders from the Ministry of Education (MOE) engaging their counterparts from the Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI) to exchange best practices on the teaching of the Malay language, literature and culture.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Just last month, the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) hosted the religious authorities from Perak, led by its Mufti Dr Wan Zahidi Wan Teh, to discuss best practices regarding the generation of fatwa or religious advisories, and the management of asatizah or religious teachers.

sections.label: Singapore largest investor in Indonesia
sections.summary: Singapore has been the largest foreign investor in Indonesia since 2014, a position maintained during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore has been the largest foreign investor in Indonesia since 2014 – a position we have maintained even during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Cooperation with Batam and Bintan
sections.summary: Cooperation with Batam and Bintan has been stepped up, including new data centres and efforts to develop tech talent.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have stepped up cooperation, especially with Batam and Bintan.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This includes establishing new data centres and efforts to develop tech talent, which could support the rapidly growing tech sectors in both Singapore and Indonesia.

sections.label: Human Capital Partnership Agreement signed
sections.summary: MOE and Indonesia's Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology signed a Human Capital Partnership Agreement last year for technical and vocational education cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To accelerate digital transformation and raise skill levels, the MOE and the Indonesian Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology signed a Human Capital Partnership Agreement last year to strengthen our cooperation in technical and vocational education and training.

sections.label: Sultan visit MOUs signed
sections.summary: During the Sultan's visit, four MOUs were signed to boost cooperation in energy, green economy, trade, investment, youth education and public service.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: During the Sultan's visit, four MOUs were signed to boost cooperation in new areas such as energy and green economy, trade and investment in food and medical products, youth education scholarship and public service capacity development.

sections.label: RCEP tariff elimination
sections.summary: The RCEP, effective at the start of 2022, eliminates tariffs on about 92% of goods traded among signatory parties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The RCEP, which came into effect at the start of 2022, eliminates the tariffs of about 92% of goods traded amongst the signatory parties.

sections.label: ASEAN Smart Cities Network launch
sections.summary: The ASEAN Smart Cities Network Initiative was launched when Singapore chaired ASEAN in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Smart Cities Network Initiative (ASCN) was launched when we were chair of ASEAN in 2018.

sections.label: ASEAN Digital Economy Framework negotiations
sections.summary: ASEAN is set to commence negotiations on an ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement aiming to create a seamless digital trade ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ASEAN is set to commence negotiations on an ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) that aims to create a seamless digital trade ecosystem across the region.

sections.label: Myanmar ASEAN summit invitation level
sections.summary: ASEAN Leaders agreed at their November Summit that Myanmar will only be invited at the non-political level for ASEAN Summits and Foreign Ministers' Meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Leaders reviewed this issue at their Summit in November and agreed that Myanmar will only be invited at the non-political level for the ASEAN Summits and Foreign Ministers' Meetings.

sections.label: Singapore aid for displaced persons
sections.summary: Singapore supports ASEAN's efforts to facilitate refugees' safe return and has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral aid for displaced persons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore supports ASEAN's efforts to facilitate the refugees' safe return and has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral aid to meet the urgent humanitarian needs of displaced persons.

sections.label: PayNow India UPI linkage launch
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the linkage of Singapore's PayNow and India's Unified Payments Interface on 21 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: On 21 February 2023, Prime Minister Lee and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the linkage of the Singapore's PayNow and India's Unified Payments Interface.

sections.label: Singapore Saudi Arabia engagements
sections.summary: Prime Minister met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman at the November 2022 APEC meeting, Minister Vivian visited Saudi Arabia, and the second Saudi-Singapore Joint Committee met.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Prime Minister met the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders Meeting in November 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Minister Vivian also visited Saudi Arabia in September 2022, while the second Saudi-Singapore Joint Committee meeting was held in November 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are also glad that the Haj for 2023 has resumed without restrictions and look forward to Saudi Arabia's favourable consideration to increase our Haj quota, which was discussed during Prime Minister's meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed.

sections.label: Upgrade of diplomatic relations
sections.summary: The two countries agreed on the mutual upgrade of diplomatic relations to the Embassy level to deepen strategic and economic links.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To signal our shared commitment to deepen the strategic and economic links between our two countries, we agreed on the mutual upgrade of our diplomatic relations to the Embassy level.

sections.label: Support for two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore has supported a negotiated two-state solution allowing Israelis and Palestinians to live side-by-side in peace and security, per relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore has been steadfast in our support for a negotiated two-state solution that allows both Israelis and Palestinians to live side-by-side in peace and security, in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

sections.label: Israeli outposts legitimisation concern
sections.summary: The recent Israeli government decision to retroactively legitimise nine outposts in the West Bank is deeply worrying.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The recent decision by the Israeli government to retroactively legitimise nine outposts in the West Bank is deeply worrying.

sections.label: Singapore-China JCBC cooperation
sections.summary: The JCBC platform concluded 19 deliverables at the 18th JCBC, and the Suzhou, Tianjin and Chongqing projects continue, with the Tianjin Eco City's 15th anniversary this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our apex bilateral cooperation platform, the JCBC, continues to reflect the breadth and depth of Singapore-China cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We concluded 19 deliverables spanning health, sustainability, green finance, tourism, trade security and others at the 18th JCBC last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our signature government-to-government projects in Suzhou, Tianjin and Chongqing have not only withstood the test of time, but also continued to reinvent themselves in support of both our countries' development priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will leverage the 15th anniversary of the Tianjin Eco City this year to refresh our cooperation.

sections.label: Resuming exchanges with China
sections.summary: With China adjusting its pandemic management approach, in-person exchanges and visits are expected to resume this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: With China adjusting its pandemic management approach, we believe that we would be able to resume in-person exchanges and visits this year.

sections.label: Singapore-Japan cooperation memoranda
sections.summary: Singapore and Japan signed two Memoranda of Cooperation covering AI, cybersecurity and digital government transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore and Japan signed two Memoranda of Cooperation covering issues such as AI, cybersecurity and digital government transformation.

sections.label: Green Economy Framework with UK
sections.summary: A Green Economy Framework with the UK will be signed next month, and negotiations on a Singapore-UK Investment Protection Agreement are being pursued.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, we will sign a Green Economy Framework with the UK next month, and we are also working towards launching negotiations on a Singapore-UK Investment Protection Agreement.

sections.label: Engagement of Latin America
sections.summary: Singapore reopened its Honorary Consulate-General in Lima, Peru and will open a new Honorary Consulate in Bogotá, Colombia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To deepen our engagement of Latin America, Singapore reopened our Honorary Consulate-General in Lima, Peru and will open a new Honorary Consulate in Bogotá, Colombia.

sections.label: Singapore-Africa Partnership Package
sections.summary: In Kigali, the Prime Minister announced the three-year Singapore-Africa Partnership Package offering customised courses for African officials on development priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In Kigali, Prime Minister announced the three-year Singapore-Africa Partnership Package, offering customised courses for African officials to address their development priorities in areas, such as climate change, digitalisation and smart cities.

sections.label: NRAs and diplomatic outreach
sections.summary: Singapore's 46 NRAs accredited to 48 countries and four International Organisations amplify diplomatic outreach and nurture ties with partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our 46 NRAs accredited to 48 countries and four International Organisations amplify Singapore's diplomatic outreach and nurture our ties with various partners, especially in places where we do not have a diplomatic mission.

sections.label: Foreign officials in SCP
sections.summary: Close to 150,000 foreign officials have taken part in the SCP, with courses continually adjusted to developing countries' evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Close to 150,000 foreign officials have taken part in the SCP and we have continually adjusted our courses to respond to the evolving needs of developing countries.

sections.label: Documents of Identity issued
sections.summary: In 2022, MFA facilitated the issuance of 730 Documents of Identity, a temporary travel document for Singaporeans who lost passports overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2022, MFA facilitated the issuance of 730 Documents of Identity, a temporary travel document for Singaporeans who have lost their passports overseas to travel home.

sections.label: Improving consular services
sections.summary: MFA continually reviews processes, launched online Document of Identity applications, and established a consular corps of professional first responders for 24/7 assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To ensure that MFA continues to deliver prompt and effective consular services to overseas Singaporeans, we continually review and improve on our processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have harnessed digital technology to launch online applications for Documents of Identity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have also established a new consular corps of professional first responders to provide 24/7 consular response and assistance to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Women in foreign service
sections.summary: Half of Singapore's foreign service is made up of women.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Half of Singapore's foreign service is made up of women.

sections.label: Foreign influence and consensus
sections.summary: Singaporeans must not be unwitting vectors of foreign influence, domestic politics stops at the border, and consensus is forged on foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singaporeans must be aware of this danger and not be unwitting vectors of foreign influence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our domestic politics stops at the border and we forge consensus on our foreign policy.

sections.label: Singapore not a proxy
sections.summary: Singapore cannot say one thing in Beijing and another in Washington, and is not a stalking horse or proxy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think we should also know our place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We are not going to be able to bring them together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But what I would say is, as a representative of Singapore, I do not have the luxury of saying one thing in Beijing and then a different thing in Washington.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, both Beijing and Washington know that when we analyse the situation and we take a decision, it is not for one side or the other.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We are not a stalking horse, we are not a proxy.

sections.label: Engaging superpowers posture
sections.summary: The speaker says thinking straight, being consistent and clear is a useful way to engage superpowers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Taking this kind of posture – thinking straight, being consistent, being very clear where we come from – in fact, I have found to be a very good and useful way to engage superpowers.

sections.label: Singapore declining ASEAN meeting
sections.summary: The member asks the Minister to confirm Singapore's reasons for not attending a meeting, along with other founding ASEAN members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I understood that Singapore declined to attend, together with, perhaps, the other founding members of ASEAN – the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, two questions concerning this: one, could the Minister confirm our reasons for not wanting to attend this meeting?

sections.label: ASEAN Five-Point Consensus Myanmar
sections.summary: The April 2021 Jakarta meeting created the Five-Point Consensus, and later Myanmar was barred from political-level ASEAN meetings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In April 2021, when our Leaders met in Jakarta – there was a special ASEAN meeting called for that – that was the meeting that created the Five-Point Consensus, the consensus amongst the ASEAN Leaders present.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Later on that year, we decided that Myanmar will not participate at a political level in ASEAN meetings.

sections.label: No Myanmar political representation
sections.summary: Leaders met in November and reaffirmed that summits and Foreign Ministers' meetings shall have no political representation from Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our Leaders met again in November and reaffirmed this decision, that at the summit and at meetings of Foreign Ministers, there shall be no political representation from Myanmar.

sections.label: Views on Myanmar junta
sections.summary: The speaker says he tells the junta Singapore's views, will not interfere, and suggests sticking to the Five-Point Consensus and releasing detainees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But have I spoken to the people in the junta in the past?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I will tell them what our views are and that we will not interfere, but we do not want to make things worse and our suggestion is – stick to the Five-Point Consensus, release the political detainees, allow Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and President U Win Myint to sit down at a table and discuss the future with the military authorities in Myanmar.

sections.label: Review of UNHCR contributions
sections.summary: The member says it is not being done now and asks when the next review of contributions to UNHCR is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I think the reply is that we are not doing it now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, could I just ask when is the next review for our contributions to UNHCR?

sections.label: Myanmar national reconciliation solution
sections.summary: The real solution is national reconciliation and peace within Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The real solution is national reconciliation and peace within Myanmar.

sections.label: ASEAN Humanitarian Assistance Package
sections.summary: The ASEAN Humanitarian Assistance Package has a centre sending teams to do needs assessment, and Singapore may step up assistance based on their reports.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For instance, we have the ASEAN Humanitarian Assistance Package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have a centre that sends teams on the ground to do needs assessment and depending on their reports, we will be prepared, if necessary, to step up assistance to the people on the ground in Myanmar.

sections.label: ASEAN Summit vote question
sections.summary: The member asks for clarity on whether Singapore has pushed at the ASEAN Summit for a vote where consensus is impossible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: However, I would like more clarity on the Minister's answers to my questions just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I asked, has Singapore ever pushed at the ASEAN Summit for a decision to be taken, by a vote, on issues where arriving at a consensus is impossible?

sections.label: Alternative ASEAN decision-making mechanisms
sections.summary: The member asks whether Singapore is open to considering alternative decision-making mechanisms at ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: More fundamentally, is Singapore open to considering alternative decision-making mechanisms at ASEAN?

sections.label: ASEAN Five-Point Consensus decision
sections.summary: The decision on the ASEAN Five-Point Consensus was made at that meeting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as far as we are concerned, the decision on the ASEAN Five-Point Consensus was made at that meeting.

sections.label: Myanmar not holding ASEAN hostage
sections.summary: Singapore has not allowed Myanmar to hold it hostage or force it to expedite recognising the coup outcome.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: More importantly, we have not allowed Myanmar to hold us hostage and force us to expedite, for instance, recognising the coup outcome so that we can conduct business as usual.

sections.label: ASEAN Charter consensus exceptions
sections.summary: The ASEAN Charter envisages occasions where consensus will not be possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, the ASEAN Charter does envisage that there will be occasions where consensus will not be possible.

sections.label: Development work compliance and proceeding
sections.summary: Development work is necessary, complies with international law and rights, and will proceed in due course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Just to reiterate what I had said just now, we are sure that our development work is necessary and that it is fully in compliance with international law and our rights, and we will proceed in due course.
